conclusions: The exact historical column sequence is sufficient for the modern tax-zero case but not for the complete carbon-tax continuation.
A fresh modern tax-zero solution can match headline archived metrics while leading the next tax step to a different local optimum; checkpoint-level state differences remain numerically consequential.
Reloading the exact archived tax-zero state closely recovers the USD 0.01/tonne result, demonstrating that initialization state is causal for that transition.
The USD 1/tonne transition is not reproduced from its exact preceding archived checkpoint with MA27, MA57, or MA57 internal automatic scaling under the tested 100-iteration policy.

The identical nl and nl_v1 MA27 traces reject the remaining writer-selection hypothesis for the USD 1/tonne failure. Representation-robust state scaling and checkpoint-state comparison are the next diagnostics.
